articles.title: Why a Good AI Product May Be the Wrong Venture Bet
articles.summary: Nan Zhou on fund economics, founder judgment, and the difference between seeing an opportunity and being able to invest.
takeaways: Fund size changes what a good investment looks like. A useful, profitable product can be an attractive business and still be too small for a particular fund's return requirements.
Conviction starts with a hypothesis and earns its credibility through risk analysis. A technical insight must survive questions about the market, engineering, team, timing, and execution.
Founder quality becomes visible over time. Zhou's examples include Scale AI's response to a changing customer market and the engineers who followed Cerebras's founder into another difficult company.

articles.title: When 400 AI Agents Need One Human
articles.summary: Jinjing Liang on the engineering of delegation, model neutrality, and the work behind Orca.
takeaways: Parallel AI work creates a coordination problem: persistent task context, checkpoints, and clear handoffs matter as much as execution.
Keep people involved where judgment is needed. Agents should pause at material ambiguity and return a concrete result that a person can review.
A small team can shorten the path from a real user problem to a shipped improvement, while model choice and continuity remain valuable.
